newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.N. SECRETARY GENERAL TOURS MANDELA'S ISLAND JAIL.
newsitem.headline: U.N. SECRETARY GENERAL TOURS MANDELA'S ISLAND JAIL.

text.p: United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan toured President Nelson Mandela's island jail on Friday, Human Rights Day in South Africa.

Ushered around the jail on Robben Island where Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years as a political prisoner by Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister Aziz Pahad and a schoolteacher who also served time, Annan inspected the tiny cell with single bed and desk.
Praising Mandela and other political prisoners' fortitude after his tour, the new U.N. boss told reporters: "It's quite a moving experience."

"To see the tenacity of the human spirit and for men to go through that and survive and come out strong, determined and unbroken, and also forgiving, is a remarkable lesson for all of us," Annan said.
His island guide, teacher Eddie Daniels, thanked Annan for the international community's pressure against past apartheid governments.

"We would have won our war -- It was a just cause. But it would have taken us so much longer. Because of the wonderful assistance we received from the whole world, it helped us get to our goal so much quicker," Daniels said.

Annan, on his first visit to Africa as head of the United Nations, is due in Angola on Saturday where the U.N. is trying to speed up the installation of a government of national unity in order to formally end 19 years of civil war.
